findings.evidence: Figure 6.1 shows a box labelled "Workload metrics rps · token profile · concurrency". Its caption states: "Figure-art note: the third printed entry in the workload box (concurrency) is an erratum in the figure art for the offered request rate λ; it is not a workload metric."
findings.issue: Figure 6.1's workload box still lists "concurrency" as a workload metric, directly contradicting §6.1.1 (page 121), which states "Concurrency is not a workload input: it is a serving-side quantity derived from the arrival rate and the time in system (Little's law), so it belongs with queue depth on the scheduler side, not in this layer." The caption acknowledges the error rather than fixing the art, so the figure continues to teach the wrong classification at a glance.
findings.fix_instruction: Regenerate Figure 6.1's workload box to read "rps · token profile" only (matching Fig. 6.1's own stated intent), and remove the erratum sentence from the caption once the art is corrected.

findings.evidence: "Suppose ... p50 TTFT might sit at ~1.0 s."
findings.issue: The ~1.0 s p50 TTFT is a value computed from canonical-scenario inputs (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~0.88 s ≈ 1.0 s) and feeds the subsequent p95 drift calculation, yet carries no evidence label. Per the Preface rule, a load-bearing quantitative value that later calculation depends on must be labeled [canonical scenario][DERIVED]. The surrounding paragraph has labels for other quantities but this one is bare.
findings.fix_instruction: Add [canonical scenario][DERIVED] after '~1.0 s' in the paragraph describing the flash-crowd p50/p95 TTFT scenario.

findings.evidence: Fig. 6.1 caption, PDF p.146: "Figure-art note: the third printed entry in the workload box (concurrency) is an erratum in the figure art for the offered request rate λ; it is not a workload metric. Concurrency proper is derived on the serving side (in-flight = λ × W, Little's law), the same classification this figure gives queue depth; see §6.1.1."  And §6.1.1, PDF p.144: "Concurrency is not a workload input: it is a serving-side quantity derived from the arrival rate and the time in system (Little's law), so it belongs with queue depth on the scheduler side, not in this layer."
findings.issue: The rendered Fig. 6.1 artwork still prints 'concurrency' inside the 'Workload metrics' box, directly contradicting §6.1.1's classification and the figure's own causal chain (workload → resource → serving). The defect is patched only in the caption prose, so the figure itself — the artifact most readers will extract, redraw, or cite — carries the wrong taxonomy entry. The book treats this figure as the spine of its diagnostic method (Ch. 6 is the metrics chapter; Fig. 6.1 is referenced from Ch. 12's optimization map and the pattern library), so an unfixed artwork error propagates.
findings.fix_instruction: Regenerate Fig. 6.1 so the workload box lists the offered quantities only (rps / request rate λ, token profile), and either move 'in-flight requests (λ·W)' into the serving box next to queue depth or drop it. Then delete the 'Figure-art note' erratum sentence from the caption, so the figure and its legend no longer disagree. If the artwork cannot be regenerated for this edition, restate the erratum as a visible on-figure footnote rather than caption text only.
